title: Immediate Steps After a Car Accident in Boston, Massachusetts
metaDescription: Learn the immediate steps to take after a car accident in Boston, MA, including essential safety and legal considerations. Stay informed and prepared.
excerpt: Educational Boston, MA guide — 3-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: First 10 minutes: safety and 911
paragraphs: A collision on I-95 or surface streets in Boston can escalate quickly. If vehicles are drivable and it is safe, move to a shoulder or parking lot. Turn on hazard lights.
Call 911 when anyone reports pain, airbags deploy, fluids leak, or traffic is blocked. Boston County dispatch will route Boston police or state patrol depending on location.
list: Stay inside the vehicle with seatbelts on if traffic passes closely at highway speed
Do not admit fault — describe facts only
Request a crash report number before officers leave

sections.heading: Boston documentation checklist
paragraphs: Photograph all vehicles, license plates, VIN stickers, skid marks, traffic signals, and visible injuries. Boston insurers expect timestamped photos.
Collect names and phone numbers from witnesses — independent accounts matter on I-95, I-75 and in Boston County.
Exchange insurance policy numbers and registration; note employer if the other driver was working.

sections.heading: Medical care within 24 hours
paragraphs: Boston has Boston Regional Medical Center and Boston General Hospital among its major facilities. Level I trauma care is available at Boston Level I Trauma Center.
Whiplash, concussion, and internal injuries may appear hours later. A same-day urgent care or ER visit creates a medical record insurers cannot easily dismiss.

sections.heading: Massachusetts reporting rules
paragraphs: Massachusetts requires crash reporting when injuries, death, or significant property damage occur. Minimum liability limits are 20/40/5.

Cooperate with officers; request a copy of the report through the investigating agency. If police do not respond, check https://www.mass.gov/orgs/massachusetts-department-of-transportation for self-report thresholds.

sections.heading: Insurance notification without hurting your claim
paragraphs: Notify your carrier with basic facts — date, location, vehicles involved. Decline recorded statements until you understand your coverage and injuries.
Massachusetts no-fault rules may limit lawsuits unless injuries exceed thresholds — verify with counsel.

sections.heading: Evidence preservation in Boston
paragraphs: Dashcam, Ring doorbell, and business security footage near Boston downtown interchange is often deleted within 7–30 days. Send written preservation letters when appropriate.
Save repair estimates, rental receipts, and mileage to medical appointments.

sections.heading: When to explore attorney matching
paragraphs: Consider a free consultation if you were hospitalized, fault is disputed, a commercial vehicle was involved, or the adjuster offers a quick settlement before treatment finishes.
WreckMatch LLC connects Boston residents with licensed Massachusetts attorneys — we are a referral service, not a law firm.

sections.heading: Boston medical resources after a crash
paragraphs: Boston residents often use Boston Regional Medical Center, Boston General Hospital after serious collisions. Level I trauma care is available at Boston Level I Trauma Center.
Document every provider visit — gaps in treatment are a common reason MA insurers reduce settlement offers.
Keep receipts for prescriptions, imaging (MRI/CT), physical therapy, and medical transport.
list: Photograph visible injuries the same day when safe
Follow discharge instructions and keep all after-visit summaries
Do not sign blanket medical authorizations for the adjuster

sections.heading: Local crash patterns: I-95, I-75
paragraphs: The metro area sees roughly 6,422 reported crashes annually (est.). High-risk areas include Boston downtown interchange; Major highway corridor near Boston.
If your collision occurred near I-95, note mile markers, exit numbers, and direction of travel for the police report.
Massachusetts DOT data is available via https://www.mass.gov/orgs/massachusetts-department-of-transportation — useful when disputing fault or road conditions.

sections.heading: Boston County reports, courts, and evidence
paragraphs: Request the official crash report through the investigating agency. Boston County Civil Court handles many civil injury filings in the region.
Business security video near Boston retail corridors is often deleted within 7–30 days — send preservation letters quickly when appropriate.
The Boston Bar Association offers lawyer-referral resources; WreckMatch LLC can also connect you with independent Massachusetts attorneys at no obligation.

sections.heading: Settlement timeline expectations in Boston
paragraphs: Minor property-damage claims in Boston may resolve in weeks, but injury claims involving treatment, lost wages, or disputed fault often take months. Insurers may request recorded statements, independent medical exams, and broad medical authorizations — review each request carefully.
Massachusetts uses 51% bar comparative negligence with a 3-year statute of limitations for most injury cases. Calendar your deadline from the date of injury.
If you were transported from I-95 to Boston Regional Medical Center, keep ambulance, ER, and follow-up bills organized. UM/UIM and MedPay endorsements may apply when the other driver is underinsured.
list: Do not accept the first settlement check if treatment is ongoing
Avoid discussing fault on social media
Request adjuster denials or reservations of rights in writing
Compare repair estimates with your insurer's appraisal
Consult a licensed attorney before signing general releases

sections.heading: Document checklist for Boston claims
paragraphs: Organize a folder (physical or digital) for every document tied to your Boston crash: police report number, insurance claim numbers, tow and storage receipts, and rental car agreements.
Request itemized medical bills from Boston Regional Medical Center rather than summary statements — itemized bills help catch billing errors and support future negotiations.
list: Photos of all vehicles and the scene from multiple angles
Employer note for any missed work shifts
Insurance adjuster name, phone, and claim number
Repair estimates from at least two body shops
